title: examples(go): update streaming consumer loop + helper for final message assembly
author: Mateusz Zielinski
description:
Context: Our Go examples still used the old “print whatever arrives” approach for streaming. That breaks down once you include tool-call deltas, content deltas, and the final assembled message (and it’s a common source of support pings when customers try to copy/paste).

This PR refreshes the Go streaming example consumer loop to match the canonical event conventions we’re aligning across Python/TS/Go:
- Treat the stream as an event sequence (content deltas, tool-call deltas, final message, and errors)
- Assemble the final assistant message deterministically (instead of assuming the last chunk is the full message)
- Log/handle partial tool arguments safely (don’t attempt JSON decode mid-stream)
- Add concise retry/disconnect notes so the example doesn’t imply “just reconnect and continue” semantics we don’t guarantee

What changed:
- New helper: AssembleFinalMessage(events) that merges content deltas + tool-call deltas into a final assistant message shape for printing/returning.
- Updated example loop to switch on event.Type and call the helper at the end.
- Improved comments around known footguns: partial args, premature JSON parsing, disconnect/retry.
- Small output changes so the example prints a stable “final” block at the end (useful for docs and smoke tests).

Why now:
- Needed for cross-SDK parity work (ENG-4821/ENG-4825) and the docs refresh.
- Addresses recurring confusion in SUP-18421: customers were parsing tool-call args on every chunk and seeing truncated JSON.

Notes/Non-goals:
- No API/protocol changes. This is example-level code + small helper in the examples package only.
- We intentionally do not add any “resume stream from last event id” sample because we don’t have a stable server-side resume guarantee.

Test plan:
- go test ./... (unit + compilation)
- Ran examples/streaming_chat locally against hosted API (manual) and verified:
  - content prints incrementally
  - tool call args are only parsed after final assembly
  - final message prints once, deterministically

Release notes:
- Go examples: updated streaming consumer loop to robustly assemble final responses; includes guidance for partial tool args and safe retry behavior.
commits: examples: refactor streaming consumer loop to switch on event types
examples: add AssembleFinalMessage helper + tests for delta merge
docs(example comments): clarify retry/disconnect + partial JSON caveats
chore: rename variables for parity with Python/TS snippets
changed_areas: README snippets (Go section) referencing streaming loop
docs comments in examples for retry/disconnect behavior
review_conversation:
Ibrahim Khan: Can we make it explicit in the example that tool-call args are not guaranteed to be valid JSON until the end? A lot of customers try to Unmarshal on every delta.

Mateusz Zielinski (author): Yep — added a comment in the tool delta case and moved all JSON parsing to after AssembleFinalMessage.

Brian Murphy: The helper currently concatenates args strings; do we need to handle “multiple tool calls” within the same response?

Mateusz Zielinski: Good catch. Updated AssembleFinalMessage to key by tool_call_id and merge args per call. Added a test with two calls in one stream.

Wei Chen: Please add a short retry note. Docs keep getting questions about reconnect semantics.

Mateusz Zielinski: Added a retry/disconnect section: we recommend retrying the *request* idempotently, not resuming mid-stream. Also added a link placeholder to the canonical streaming conventions page (docs will wire it up).

Monica Patel: Any chance this changes public SDK APIs?

Mateusz Zielinski: No public API changes; helper is under examples/internal. Streaming API usage is unchanged.

Ibrahim Khan: Approved after the multi-tool merge fix + tests.

Brian Murphy: Approved.

Monica Patel: Approved.
merge_summary: Merged via squash after adding multi-tool merge handling in AssembleFinalMessage and clarifying retry/disconnect semantics in example comments.
